reason: Prior K-loop changes passed correctness but did not meet promotion rules, so I rank the distinct counter-move schedule experiment ahead of further reduction-loop rewrites. A-transpose packing is a stronger first test because it targets work inside the timed n=512 path. Grouped stores may reduce output-store instructions, but Apple clang acceptance is unverified. Packing, traversal, and scratch-layout proposals have uncertain costs or overlapping mechanisms; B-panel packing also adds work where the current B loads are already contiguous. The fallback-only tail proposal cannot improve the timed n=512 path. All proposals remain unverified hypotheses.
